newsitem.title: DUBAI: UAE to stop illegal labour recruitment.
newsitem.headline: UAE to stop illegal labour recruitment.

text.p: A United Arab Emirates official said in remarks published on Thursday the Gulf state would soon attempt to stop illegal labour recruitment agencies.

Mohammad Essa al-Suweidi, under-secretary of the Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs, told the English-language The Gulf Today that unauthorised agencies would be severely penalised. He did not say what the penalties would be.
"We are aware that hundreds of agents are conducting clandestine operations and raking in the (profits)," he said.
"These agents collect the CVs of people who are on a visit visa and desperately need a job. Then they contact companies that need labour. This procedure is against the law."
Foreigners on visit visas to the UAE are not allowed to work in the country.

The planned move appears to be part of a campaign to restrict illegal workers. Foreigners, mostly from the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia, make up 75-80 percent of the UAE's 2.4 million population.

An estimated 200,000 illegal workers flooded out of the oil-rich state to take advantage of an amnesty and avoid penalties such as jail terms, fines and deportation before a tough new labour law came into effect on October 31.
The UAE says the growing number of illegal aliens pose a security threat to the country.
"...Several illegal recruitment agencies have stopped operating after the amnesty, as these agents will be heavily penalised and even jailed if caught," Suweidi said.
He said that even authorised agents will be penalised if they violate labour ministry laws.

He added that if a salary agreement between an employer and worker is violated, "punishment can be in the form of...not issuing further workers' visas to the employer...These actions will eventually force the company to close."
